Factor loadings table

Source: R/loadings.R
apa_loadings.Rd

Makes an APA-style table of factor loadings from an exploratory factor analysis or a principal components analysis.

Usage

apa_loadings(
  fit,
  sort_loading = TRUE,
  min_loading = 0.2,
  factor_names = NULL,
  variance = FALSE,
  communality = FALSE,
  uniqueness = FALSE,
  complexity = FALSE,
  bold_max = FALSE,
  format_variable_names = TRUE,
  digits = 2
)

Arguments

fit

a psych::fa, psych::principal, parameters::factor_analysis, or parameters::principal_components object

sort_loading

sort the rows so that variables are grouped by the factor with their largest loading, and by the size of that loading within each factor (as in psych::fa.sort())

min_loading

minimum absolute loading to display. Use NA or 0 to show all loadings.

factor_names

names for the factors. Either an unnamed character vector in the order the factors appear in the table (psych orders factors by variance explained), or a named vector that maps the original names to new names (e.g., c(PA1 = "Verbal")). The unnamed form is safer: after an oblimin rotation, the labels psych assigns (PA1, PA2, ...) can change from one run to the next, but the order of the factors does not.

variance

add rows for the variance explained by each factor

communality

add a communality (h^2^) column

uniqueness

add a uniqueness (u^2^) column

complexity

add a column with Hofmann's complexity index

bold_max

bold the largest displayed loading (in absolute value) in each row

format_variable_names

format the variable names with the Variable column format. Set to FALSE to keep item text exactly as it is.

digits

number of decimal places for loadings

Value

apa7_tbl (tibble)

Details

fit can be a psych::fa() or psych::principal() object, or the output of parameters::factor_analysis() or parameters::principal_components(). For the parameters functions, the loadings come from the underlying model, so their sort and threshold settings do not matter: use sort_loading and min_loading instead. Unrotated parameters::principal_components() output wraps a stats::prcomp() model. Its loadings are the correlations between the variables and the components when the variables are standardized (the default, standardize = TRUE).

Loadings smaller in absolute value than min_loading are left blank. With bold_max = TRUE, the largest displayed loading in each row is bolded.

Rows for variance explained (variance = TRUE) are added below the loadings: the sum of squared loadings, the proportion of total variance, and the cumulative proportion (the last only when there is more than one factor). apa_flextable() draws a rule above these rows. With an oblique rotation the factors are correlated, so the variance explained by each factor overlaps with the others and the cumulative proportion is only approximate. Report the factor correlations with apa_factor_cor().

The variable names are formatted (e.g., title case) when format_variable_names = TRUE. Either way, apa_flextable() leaves the Variable column as it is, so item text is never changed again when the table is rendered.

Examples

fit <- psych::fa(Harman74.cor$cov, 4, fm = "pa", rotate = "varimax")
apa_loadings(
  fit,
  factor_names = c("Verbal", "Spatial", "Speed", "Memory")
)
#> # A tibble: 24 × 5
#>    Variable               Verbal Spatial Speed  Memory
#>    <chr>                  <chr>  <chr>   <chr>  <chr> 
#>  1 Sentence Completion    ".81"  ""      ""     ""    
#>  2 Word Meaning           ".81"  ""      ""     ".22" 
#>  3 Pargraph Comprehension ".76"  " .21"  ""     ".23" 
#>  4 General Information    ".73"  ""      " .22" ""    
#>  5 Word Classification    ".57"  " .34"  " .23" ""    
#>  6 Visual Perception      ""     " .68"  ""     ""    
#>  7 Paper Form Board       ""     " .55"  ""     ""    
#>  8 Flags                  ".23"  " .53"  ""     ""    
#>  9 Series Completion      ".37"  " .52"  " .23" ".22" 
#> 10 Cubes                  ""     " .45"  ""     ""    
#> # ℹ 14 more rows

# With rows for variance explained and bolded primary loadings
apa_loadings(fit, variance = TRUE, communality = TRUE, bold_max = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 27 × 6
#>    Variable               PA1       PA3        PA2    PA4   `*h*^2^`
#>    <chr>                  <chr>     <chr>      <chr>  <chr> <chr>   
#>  1 Sentence Completion    "**.81**" ""         ""     ""    .73     
#>  2 Word Meaning           "**.81**" ""         ""     ".22" .74     
#>  3 Pargraph Comprehension "**.76**" " .21"     ""     ".23" .68     
#>  4 General Information    "**.73**" ""         " .22" ""    .64     
#>  5 Word Classification    "**.57**" " .34"     " .23" ""    .51     
#>  6 Visual Perception      ""        " **.68**" ""     ""    .55     
#>  7 Paper Form Board       ""        " **.55**" ""     ""    .34     
#>  8 Flags                  ".23"     " **.53**" ""     ""    .35     
#>  9 Series Completion      ".37"     " **.52**" " .23" ".22" .51     
#> 10 Cubes                  ""        " **.45**" ""     ""    .23     
#> # ℹ 17 more rows

# Principal components
psych::principal(Harman74.cor$cov, 4) |>
  apa_loadings()
#> # A tibble: 24 × 5
#>    Variable               RC1    RC3    RC2    RC4  
#>    <chr>                  <chr>  <chr>  <chr>  <chr>

#>  2 Word Meaning           " .84" ""     ""     ""   
#>  3 Pargraph Comprehension " .81" ""     ""     ".21"
#>  4 General Information    " .79" ""     " .22" ""   
#>  5 Word Classification    " .64" " .31" " .24" ""   
#>  6 Problem Reasoning      " .42" " .41" ""     ".29"
#>  7 Visual Perception      ""     " .71" " .23" ""   
#>  8 Paper Form Board       ""     " .66" ""     ""   
#>  9 Flags                  " .25" " .62" ""     ""   
#> 10 Cubes                  ""     " .59" ""     ""   
#> # ℹ 14 more rows

# parameters output
parameters::principal_components(mtcars[, 1:7], n = 2) |>
  apa_loadings()
